title: tool: trim trailing URL separators in linear time
body:
With `curl -O`, a URL ending in a long run of `/` or `\` makes filename selection rescan the remaining path after removing each separator. Trim the entire suffix in one pass, then search once for the final path component. Root paths still use the default filename, and mixed slash/backslash handling is retained.

Existing test 1639 now supplies a URL with 60,000 trailing slashes through a test config file, keeping command lines short, and checks the downloaded file name and contents. Test 1644 continues to cover a path component followed by trailing slashes. Both tests pass in a debug CMake build. This is a command-line CPU-efficiency fix; the test covers the long-input behavior but does not assert a runtime threshold.

files.patch:
@@ -33,15 +33,18 @@ http
 <name>
 -O with URL without path using many trailing slashes
 </name>
+<file name="%LOGDIR/test%TESTNUMBER.config">
+url = "http://%HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT%repeat[60000 x /]%"
+</file>
 <command option="no-output">
-http://%HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT///////////////// -O --output-dir %LOGDIR
+-K %LOGDIR/test%TESTNUMBER.config -O --output-dir %LOGDIR
 </command>
 </client>
 
 # Verify data after the test has been "shot"
 <verify>
 <protocol crlf="headers">
-GET ///////////////// HTTP/1.1
+GET %repeat[60000 x /]% HTTP/1.1
 Host: %HOSTIP:%HTTPPORT
 User-Agent: curl/%VERSION
 Accept: */*
